chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Jārūd, from Mūsā ibn Bakr ibn Dāb, from one who narrated it to him, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام came to Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, carrying letters from the people of al-Kūfah, inviting him to themselves, informing him of their gathering, and commanding him to rise.

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “Are these letters an initiative from them, or a response to what you wrote to them and invited them toward?” He said: “Rather, they are an initiative from the people, because of their recognition of our right, our kinship to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, what they find in the Book of Allah عز وجل regarding the obligation of loving us and the duty of obeying us, and because of the hardship, distress, and affliction in which we are.”

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “Obedience is an obligation from Allah عز وجل, and a sunnah (prophetic tradition) that He established among the former ones, and likewise He causes it to proceed among the latter ones. Obedience is to one of us, while love is for all of us. The command of Allah proceeds for His awliyāʾ by a connected judgment, a decisive decree, a determined inevitability, an apportioned measure, and an appointed term at a known time.”
“So do not let those who have no certainty make light of you; surely they will never avail you against Allah in anything.”

“So do not be hasty, for Allah does not hasten because of the hastening of the servants, and do not try to precede Allah, lest the affliction overpower you and strike you down.” He said: Zayd became angry at that, then said: “The Imam from among us is not one who sits in his house, lets down his curtain, and discourages from jihad, but rather the Imam from among us is one who protects his domain, strives in the way of Allah with the striving due to it, defends his subjects, and guards his sanctuary.”

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “O my brother, do you know within yourself anything of what you have ascribed to it, such that you may bring for it a witness from the Book of Allah, or a proof from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, or set forth an example by it? Allah عز وجل has made halal (permissible) what is halal, made haram (forbidden) what is haram, imposed obligations, set forth parables, and established sunnahs, and He did not make the Imam who rises by His command doubtful concerning what He imposed for him of obedience, such that he should precede a matter before its proper place or strive in it before its arrival.”
And Allah عز وجل has said regarding hunting: “Do not kill game while you are in the state of iḥrām.”
“Is killing game greater, or killing the soul which Allah has forbidden? And He has made for everything a proper place.”
And Allah عز وجل said: “And when you come out of iḥrām, then hunt.”
And He عز وجل said: “Do not violate the symbols of Allah, nor the sacred month.”
So He made the months a known number, and from them He made four sacred.
And He said: “So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot frustrate Allah.”
Then He, Blessed and Exalted, said: “Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them.”
So He made for that a proper place.
And He said: “And do not resolve upon the marriage tie until the prescribed term reaches its end.”
So He made for everything an appointed term, and for every term a decree.

“So if you are upon a clear proof from your Lord, certainty in your affair, and clarification regarding your matter, then proceed with your matter. Otherwise, do not seek a matter concerning which you are in doubt and uncertainty, and do not attempt the removal of a dominion whose fruit has not yet ended, whose extent has not yet been cut off, and whose decree has not yet reached its appointed term. For if its extent had been reached, its fruit cut off, and the decree had reached its term, the separation would have ended, the order would have followed in sequence, and Allah would have made humiliation and abasement follow upon the follower and the followed alike.”

“I seek refuge in Allah from an Imam who strays from his time, such that the follower in it is more knowledgeable than the one followed. O my brother, do you wish to revive the creed of a people who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, disobeyed His Messenger, followed their desires without guidance from Allah, and claimed the caliphate without any proof from Allah nor covenant from His Messenger? I place you under Allah’s protection, O my brother, lest tomorrow you be the one crucified at al-Kunāsah.” Then his eyes overflowed and his tears flowed, then he said: “Allah is between us and the one who tore our veil, denied us our right, disclosed our secret, ascribed us to other than our grandfather, and said about us what we did not say about ourselves.”

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: an appointed term fixed for a known time
key_terms.الطَّاعَةُ: obedience owed by divine obligation to the rightful authority
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the divinely designated leader whose authority is binding
key_terms.الْخِلَافَةَ: the claim to rulership or succession
key_terms.الْمَوَدَّةُ: loving devotion owed to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٍ: clear proof or manifest evidence from Allah
key_terms.شُبْهَةٍ: doubt or ambiguity in undertaking a matter
key_terms.قَدَرٍ مَقْدُورٍ: a divinely measured decree determined by Allah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about the timing of uprising and the authority of the Imam in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a dialogue between Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and Zayd ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning uprising, Imamate, and the necessity of acting only at the divinely appointed time. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام argues that obedience to the Imam is governed by Allah’s decree, measured term, and explicit proof, and he supports this by citing Qur’anic examples showing that every command has its proper time and place. The passage is significant for its treatment of Imamate, divine decree, and legitimate religious authority within a historical and theological setting.
